title: The Glory of the New Covenant
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Fading Glory of the Old Covenant
subpoints: The Mosaic covenant was glorious in its origin and divine institution.
It served as a ministry of death and condemnation due to human sinfulness.
The temporary nature of Moses' shining face symbolized the passing glory of the law.

outline.title: The Surpassing Glory of the New Covenant
subpoints: The ministry of the Spirit exceeds the ministry of the letter in glory.
The new covenant brings righteousness rather than condemnation.
The glory of the new covenant is permanent, unlike the fading glory of the old.

outline.title: The Revealed Glory of the New Testament
subpoints: The veil that blinded the minds of Israel is removed in Christ.
The reading of the Old Testament is clarified through the lens of the New Covenant.
Christ reveals the true intent and fulfillment of the law.

outline.title: The Liberating Glory of the New Covenant
subpoints: The Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit is, there is liberty.
Believers are freed from the condemnation of the law.
Freedom is found in turning to the Lord rather than relying on performance.

outline.title: The Transforming Glory of the New Covenant
subpoints: Believers behold the glory of the Lord with unveiled faces.
The Spirit transforms believers into the image of Christ.
This transformation is an ongoing process from glory to glory.

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro explores 2 Corinthians 3, addressing the perennial church struggles of legalism and antinomianism. He argues that both extremes fail to grasp the full counsel of God, whereas the Apostle Paul presents the New Covenant as the solution that surpasses the Old. The message highlights that while the Mosaic covenant was glorious in its origin and divine institution, it was ultimately a temporary administration that revealed sin and pointed toward Christ. Because human sinfulness broke the old covenant, it functioned as a ministry of death and condemnation, a reality symbolized by the fading glory of Moses' face.

The sermon contrasts this with the New Covenant, which is characterized by a surpassing and permanent glory. Through the ministry of the Spirit, the New Covenant brings life, righteousness, and clarity. The veil that previously blinded the minds of Israel is removed in Christ, allowing believers to understand the Scriptures with new clarity. This revelation leads to the liberating glory of the Spirit, where true freedom is found not in the performance of man-made rules or the rejection of all norms, but in a relationship with the Lord.

Finally, the message concludes with the transforming power of the New Covenant. Believers, with unveiled faces, behold the glory of the Lord and are being transformed into His image from glory to glory. This ongoing work of the Spirit ensures that the Christian life is not a static performance but a dynamic journey of sanctification, reflecting the eternal glory of God rather than the temporary shadows of the past.
